Disable automatic subscription updates in Settings and refresh subscriptions manually. After every refresh, review every group, primary and backup order before relying on it. Manual refresh can immediately change an active session’s routes. If you need to review changes before using them, stop Live Routing before refreshing, inspect the groups, then reconnect.

DO NOT use Live Routing if your provider returns configurations in random order. Manual refresh does NOT fix randomized ordering.

Subscription profile IDs are positional, not permanent server identities. If the provider reorders configurations, the same ID can refer to a different server, even when no member appears missing. Names alone do not prove identity.

A missing member rejects the new configuration instead of choosing a replacement. A running session can keep its last-applied configuration while the database already contains newer profiles. A local save is not a runtime acknowledgement. If status says settings differ, review the subscription and groups, then check Connect; do not assume a displayed profile is the server currently in use.

1. Import the profiles you need and check that subscription ordering is stable. Disable automatic subscription refresh.
2. Add a named group and choose its members, including members from different subscriptions if needed.
3. Keep the existing Select, Random or Round robin strategy. Availability checks are optional and off by default. For health-enabled Select, choose a primary and explicitly arrange numbered backups.
4. Choose the default group for a Live Routing connection. Add rules for apps, domains or both, choose each target and arrange rules from specific to general.
5. Save. In Connect, start Live Routing without selecting a profile, or use a regular profile connection with these rules on top.
6. Check Connect for errors and inspect the group status. The preferred primary is configuration; the runtime label shows what new connections can actually use. Unsaved picker edits are not active.

In an independent Live Routing connection, at least one group is required. Its default group carries unmatched proxy traffic and Core Routing proxy targets. Until you choose a default explicitly, the first group is used. Core Routing direct and block rules still handle traffic not already matched by a live rule.

With a regular profile connection, Default route refers to the selected profile instead. Live rules may still target other groups. A matching live rule targeting Default route chooses that connection proxy destination immediately; later Core Routing rules are not evaluated for that flow. Unmatched traffic continues through Core Routing and the connection default.

Groups reuse outbound paths, including their dependencies, not the whole member configuration. Member inbounds, DNS and unrelated routing settings do not replace the settings of the connection.

Select without availability checks uses the configured member; it does not test it or automatically fail over. Random and Round robin keep their normal per-new-connection behavior when checks are off.

With checks enabled, Select tries the configured primary first, then backups in their explicit numbered order, choosing the first eligible member. A healthy backup can be used while the primary is still unknown. A recovered primary or higher-priority backup is preferred again after its recovery threshold.

For Random and Round robin, availability is a filter, not a priority system: every eligible member participates. Random chooses among them; Round robin cycles through them. There is no single active node and list order does not create primary/backup tiers.

App only: choose a browser, leave domains empty and target a browsing group. Its traffic reaching the VPN matches regardless of domain.

Domain only: leave apps empty and enter example.com to match that domain and its subdomains. Use full:example.com for that exact name only.

App AND domain: choose a video app and enter domain:example.com. The rule matches only connections from that app to that domain or its subdomains. Other domains from the same app continue to later rules.

Order matters: put a specific app-and-domain block rule above a broader app-to-group rule. Otherwise the broader rule wins first. Multiple apps within the app list are alternatives, as are multiple domains within the domain list.

Failover: configure A as primary, B as backup 1 and C as backup 2 with checks enabled. If A becomes unavailable, new connections use B if eligible, otherwise C. If all are unknown or down, the group blocks new traffic; it never escapes through a different default group.

Checks start immediately and attempt an HTTP GET to the Ping Address configured in Settings through each exact member outbound path. This must be a valid HTTP(S) URL; the manual ping type does not change this HTTP check. Only HTTP 2xx is success; redirects are not followed. Probe starts are scheduled every 10 seconds per member when a worker slot is available, with a 5-second timeout and at most four probes running globally, so large groups can queue. User connections do not trigger extra probes.

A node starts unknown and ineligible; its first successful check makes it eligible. An eligible node becomes unavailable after two consecutive failures. An unavailable node needs three consecutive successes to return. Observations older than 35 seconds expire to unknown and require three successes again. The displayed state already includes these thresholds, so a single recent failure does not immediately mark a healthy node down.

Without queuing, detecting an outage takes roughly 10–25 seconds and confirming recovery roughly 20–35 seconds after restoration; queues can add delay. These are not per-connection timeouts. Unknown is not healthy. While there is no eligible member, including startup and controller errors, new traffic to that group is blocked. There is no direct or default-route fallback. Choose an appropriate test URL and allow time for checks and recovery.

A successful HTTP check proves only that this HTTP test worked through that outbound at that moment. It is not a full TCP/UDP test and does not guarantee that every website, DNS request, app or protocol will work. A blocked or failing test endpoint can make otherwise usable nodes unavailable. The test endpoint sees repeated requests; checks consume traffic and battery.\n\nHealth changes and saved routing updates affect new routing decisions. Established connections keep their existing paths; they are not migrated, replayed or retried automatically. An app may need to open a new connection to use a recovered primary or a backup. Turning checks off restores ordinary unchecked strategy behavior, not a promise of availability.
Draft, saved plan and running plan

A picker changes the draft only after OK. Save stores the plan locally and asks an active session to apply it. Saving does not reconnect, change connection mode or prove that the core accepted the update. Open Connect if an update fails.\n\nStatus is matched against the strategy, preferred member, ordered membership and the configuration fingerprint of every member. If the draft is unsaved, the runtime differs, a profile changed after refresh or status cannot be read, the editor will not label a current database entry as active. A group may also be loaded without any rule currently sending traffic to it. Healthy and eligible do not mean that an established connection is using that member.
App identity is not an app name

App matching requires Android 10 or newer, VPN mode with owner identification and authenticated local SOCKS. In SOCKS-only mode, use domain rules. Live Routing is unavailable in transparent root mode and this screen cannot save in that mode.

Managed UID accounts share the local SOCKS password. A direct SOCKS client holding that password can claim a managed app identity: routing is not an authorization boundary against that client. Do not share the credentials with untrusted clients.

Live Routing does not disable inbound authentication, Apps Routing or owner-protection policy. Real TUN flows pass admission checks before receiving a SOCKS identity. Traffic rejected or excluded by those mechanisms cannot be recovered by adding a Live Routing rule. Unknown owners do not satisfy app criteria. Clear app criteria from enabled rules before saving in a mode that cannot match apps.

Off: app split routing is disabled. All user app traffic goes through the VPN.

Exclude selected apps: the apps you choose bypass the VPN, and all other apps continue using the VPN.

Include only selected apps: only the apps you choose use the VPN, and all other apps bypass it.

Use Off when you want one simple full-device tunnel. Use Exclude when most apps should stay inside the tunnel and only a few should bypass it. Use Include when the VPN is needed only for a small set of apps.

The <> button formats JSON without changing its values. Syntax is checked automatically: tap the red status at the bottom to move to the reported error.

The symbol row inserts punctuation and indents or outdents text. The three-dot menu controls font size and line wrapping.

Profile details (the sliders button) contains the name and group. The top checkmark saves the profile and checks the generated configuration with Xray. Valid JSON alone does not guarantee a valid Xray configuration.
